notes: Demo of the gated two-part shape Sarah described for the EVP role: Part 1 must be submitted before Part 2 is seen, and the Part 1 decision selects which of three Part 2 tasks the candidate gets. Part 3 is the same for everyone. Placeholder wording throughout; replace it in the builder before this goes near a real candidate.

rules.lead: You can use AI and a calculator.
rules.text: We are an AI-forward organization and we would rather see how you work with the tools you actually use.

rules.lead: If you run low on time, do not try to finish everything.
rules.text: Instead, explain what other main steps you would take, and leave the rest unfinished. We would much rather read that than a rushed attempt at completeness.
Open the link in the brief, work in your own copy in another tab, and come back here to write up or attach what you produced.

sections.heading: What we are looking for
sections.text: When you are communicating internally with our team, we value clarity, brevity, and reasoning transparency over formal or academic prose. We are less interested in the perfect answer than in seeing clearly described logic, well-stated uncertainties, and a strong knack for discerning which information is the highest priority.

sections.heading: Ambiguity is deliberate
sections.text: Some aspects of this task are intentionally vague and require you to apply judgement. Where something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and label it. You do not need to email us to ask.

intro.closing: Please do not share this task with anyone outside Evidence Action / 2AI. If you need a different format or an accommodation because of a disability, write to us before you begin and we will sort it out:

outro.closing: Our team aims to review submissions within 5 business days, and successful candidates will be invited to a follow-up interview that references this work. If anything went wrong while you were working, write to us:

sections.summary: Read the data and make the call

sections.label: Part 2
sections.summary: Build out the decision you made

blocks.text: Placeholder scenario. A program has been running in one country for two years. The results are good but not uniformly so, the budget for next year is roughly flat, and the country team has asked for a decision before the next planning round.

blocks.label: Slack from your manager, 9:05am
blocks.text: Morning! Can you look at the numbers and tell me what we should do next year. I can see three ways to go and I do not mind which, but I do want to know why, and I want the reasoning written down somewhere I can forward.
Work in your own copy of the data. You can write your answer here, or attach it as a PDF or Word document, whichever suits you better.

hold.heading: You chose to keep the program as it is

grow.heading: You chose to grow the program in country

blocks.text: Placeholder. Your manager agrees, and now wants to know what growing actually costs and what has to be true for it to work.

expand.heading: You chose to expand into new geographies

blocks.text: Placeholder. Your manager agrees in principle, and the first question from the funder will be why these geographies and not others.
